Human evaluation of translation quality is generally very costly and can be performed in different ways, such as Direct Assessment (DA: requiring human assessors to assign an absolute score to a translation) or Relative Ranking (RR: requiring human assessors to rank different translations).
guideline: Human assessors assign absolute scores or rank translations based on general translation quality.
Human assessors assign an absolute quality score (0‑100) or rank translations based on overall translation quality.

Direct Assessment requires human assessors to assign an absolute score (between 0 and 100) to a translation based on general translation quality. Relative Ranking requires human assessors to rank different translations based on general translation quality.
